accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: the discussion calls the Hamiltonian–zero correspondence formal, states that identifying the operator domain and establishing self-adjointness remain open, and notes that in infinite dimension biorthogonality identifies the true adjoint only with completeness of the proposed states. Conceptual interpretation: a common domain on which the boundary condition, adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness coexist is the decisive missing object; it separates symbolic similarity and formal eigenfunctions from a Hilbert–Pólya spectral theorem. Until that object is supplied, the construction does not prove spectral reality or RH. Interleaved simplicity claims require additional correspondence assumptions and are conservatively omitted.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Unifies several local caveats into the controlling operator-domain proof burden for the entire construction.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the obstruction is prose-stable, mathematically decisive, and provides controlling context without importing the interleaved stronger claims.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source explicitly labels the argument formal, calls the domain difficult and open, names self-adjointness as future work, and states the extra completeness requirement in infinite dimension.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The hope that future self-adjointness work proves RH is source speculation; no completeness, domain, spectral-reality, or RH result is asserted here.
